nodes.name: NieSeFe alloy electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Cu plate (10 mm × 10 mm × 1 mm) and nickel plate (20 mm × 20 mm × 5 mm) were used as cathode and anode (see Fig. S1 in ESI), respectively. Before the direct-current electrodeposition, all non-working surface was insulated. The Cu plate was first mechanically polished with various grades of sandpaper (up to 800 grit) and degreased for 5 min with acetone. After that, Cu plate was immersed in the 10 wt% HCl for 5 min to activate the surface. The NieSeFe alloy was electrodeposited from a solution composed of 100 g L⁻¹ NiSO₄·6H₂O + 25 g L⁻¹ FeSO₄·7H₂O + 140 g L⁻¹ CH₄N₂S + 20 g L⁻¹ H₃BO₃ + 35 g L⁻¹ NaCl + 70 g L⁻¹ Na₃C₆H₅O₇·2H₂O. The pH value of this solution was adjusted to 4.0 with addition of some drops of 5 wt% HCl solution. The electrodeposition was performed at a current density of 2 A dm⁻² for 60 min at 40 °C with mechanical stirring (ω = 10 rpm).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows characteristic Ni peaks at 44.4° and 51.9° (JCPDS No. 04-0850) for both NieSeFe and NieS alloys. Peak broadening and preferred orientation indicate nanoscale structure, poor crystallinity, and refined grain size (3.1 nm for NieSeFe vs 5.5 nm for NieS); no sulfide phases detected.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD patterns of NieSeFe and NieS alloys are shown in Fig. 1a. As observed, the peaks presented at 2 values of 44.4° and 51.9° correspond to the characteristic peaks of Ni (JCPDS No. 04e0850)... The crystalline sizes of NieSeFe and NieS alloys are c.a. 3.1 and 5.5 nm, respectively...

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals rough surface morphology composed of spherical particles for both alloys; NieSeFe shows small granular salients, vesicular structures, and absence of cracks indicating larger surface area and stronger substrate binding compared to NieS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The surface morphologies of NieSeFe and NieS alloys exhibit rough surface compose of spherical particles... Fig. 1d and e provide the high magnification SEM images of NieSeFe alloy.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS of NieSeFe shows Ni 2p peaks at 855.6 eV (Ni2+), 856.7 eV (Ni3+ in Ni3S2), 861.2 eV (Ni0 shakeup); S 2p peaks at 162.5 eV (S2^2-), 163.6 eV (metal-sulfur bond), 168.7 eV (surface oxidation S6+); Fe 2p peaks at 709.7 eV (Fe2+), 713.7 eV (Fe3+), 705.9 eV (Fe-S bond).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni 2p region (Fig. 2a) can be divided into three peaks. The main peaks at the 855.6 (Ni 2p3/2) and 856.7 (Ni 2p1/2) correspond to characteristic features of metallic Ni2+ and Ni3+ of Ni3S2... The Fe 2p spectrum (Fig. 2c) shows two peaks at 709.7 eV (Fe2+) and 713.7 eV (Fe3+), and another peak at 705.9 eV corresponding to the Fe-S bond.
